{{Tooltip|L|Lost}} 63–68 vs. [[2014–15 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] |assoc_coach=[[Greg Gard]] }} {{2014–15 Big Ten men's basketball standings}} The '''2014–15 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. This was [[Bo Ryan]]'s 14th and final full season as head coach at Wisconsin. The team played their home games at the [[Kohl Center]] in [[Madison, Wisconsin]] and were members of the [[Big Ten Conference]].They finished the season 36–4, 16–2 in [[2014–15 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to win the Big Ten regular season championship. They defeated [[2014–15 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]], [[2014–15 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], and [[2014–15 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] to win the [[2015 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] and earn an automatic bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. This marked the Badgers' 17th straight trip to the Tournament. In the Tournament, they defeated [[2014–15 Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball team|Coastal Carolina]] and [[2014–15 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] to advance to their second straight Sweet Sixteen. They defeated [[2014–15 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and [[2014–15 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to reach the school's fourth overall and second consecutive Final Four. By upsetting unbeaten [[2014–15 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] 71–64 in the Final Four in [[Indianapolis]], the Badgers moved on to play [[2014–15 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] in the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|National Championship Game]], going for their first title in 74 years. However, Wisconsin lost the game 68–63. ==Previous season== The [[2013–14 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Badgers]] finished the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14 season]] 30–8, 12–6 in [[2013–14 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for a second place. They lost in the semifinals in the [[2014 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]] to [[2013–14 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. They received at-large bid to the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as a No. 2 seed in the West region. They defeated [[2013–14 American Eagles men's basketball team|American]] and [[2013–14 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. They defeated [[2013–14 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] and [[2013–14 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to advance to the Final Four. However, they were eliminated by [[2013–14 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in the Final Four. ==Departures== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" ! Name !! Number !! Pos. !!
